question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer is creating a SPAN session to send a copy of all the Fabric-A VSAN 11 traffic on N5K_1 to the monitoring laptop. The configuration that presented has already been applied to Cisco UCS Manager. Which action competes the configuration?
context:
Topology: Fabric A / Fabric B each have N5K_1/N5K_3 (fc1/1, fc1/2 to LAN/SAN clouds) with e1/1-2 down to N5K_2/N5K_4. Monitoring Laptop connects between N5K_1 and N5K_3 via e1/5-6. FCoE VLAN 11-VSAN 11 on Fabric A side, FCoE VLAN 12-VSAN 12 on Fabric B side. Both N5K_2 and N5K_4 connect down to a C2XX server (Ten0/Ten1).
UCS Manager GUI: LAN / Traffic Monitoring Sessions / Fabric A / Monitor Session VSAN11-Session. Properties: Name VSAN11-Session, Admin State Enabled, Destination (blank), Admin Speed 10 Gbps, Operational State Unknown, Configuration Success Yes. Sources: Uplink Ethernet Ports.
imageNote: Diagram: LAN and SAN clouds cross-connect to Fabric A (N5K_1, N5K_2) and Fabric B (N5K_3, N5K_4); a Monitoring Laptop connects to N5K_1 and N5K_3 via e1/5-6, and a C2XX server connects to N5K_2 and N5K_4 via Ten0/Ten1.
options: Create a SAN traffic monitoring session.
Set VLAN 11 as the traffic destination.
Select VSAN 1 as the source of traffic.
theory: Monitoring VSAN traffic (Fibre Channel/FCoE at the VSAN level) requires a SAN traffic monitoring session rather than a LAN monitoring session, because VSAN, FC uplink, FC port-channel, vHBA, and storage-port sources only exist under the SAN monitoring session type in Cisco UCS Manager — LAN sessions only expose Ethernet-side sources like VLANs or vNICs. Since the requirement is to mirror all Fabric-A VSAN 11 traffic, the missing step is creating that SAN traffic monitoring session (with VSAN 11 as its source) rather than trying to reuse a LAN/VLAN-based session or a NetFlow session, which serves a different purpose (flow statistics, not full packet mirroring). (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Traffic Monitoring, SAN Traffic Monitoring Sessions)
